http.protocol: Existing benchmark production server, load/driver.mjs and page-load/validate.mjs; one Tokio worker; 3 alternating pairs per workload, open-loop rates below saturation, 1s pre-roll + 5s measurement; validate every response by exact byte SHA256; fresh server each phase

limitations: Tiny complete-request medians retain +0.7% to +2.7% (+8 to +53 ns) overhead after eliminating the allocation regressions. This is not a claim of universal zero latency overhead.

Native ordinary component counts, sizes and polls match the pre-tweak baseline. Versus main, local ErrorBoundary/Suspense retains the previously known +8 bytes per boxed allocation with no extra allocation count.
HTTP uses three alternating pairs at fixed rates below saturation; it checks latency/CPU at equal load, not maximum capacity. No cross-framework scoreboard is republished.
Single local Mac, one Tokio worker for the HTTP server; no CPU pinning. Bootstrap intervals quantify process-pair variation, not universal uncertainty.
